# Ember — a warm start for coding agents

**Persistent, queryable memory for your codebase — CLI, MCP server, and a
local web UI.**
Point Ember at a repo once; every coding agent you use (Claude Code, Cursor,
Windsurf, …) starts warm instead of cold — with hybrid-capable search, a repo
map, a mined decision log, and answers that cite `file:line`. MIT licensed,
local-first, zero native dependencies.

## The problem

Coding agents start every session cold. Architecture, conventions, and the
reasons behind past decisions get reconstructed tool call by tool call —
slowly, expensively, and often wrong. Humans carry that context implicitly.

## What Ember does

- `index_repo` — scans a repo, splits code into symbol-aware chunks, embeds
  them, and builds a **pure-TypeScript HNSW** approximate nearest-neighbour
  index. Everything persists in `<repo>/.ember/` — no database, no daemon.
  Re-indexing is incremental: per-file hashes mean unchanged files keep their
  embeddings, only new/changed files are re-embedded, and deleted files drop
  out (`--full` forces a from-scratch rebuild). A `.emberignore` file keeps
  fixtures and generated files out of the corpus.
- `search_code` — ranked `file:line` hits for natural-language queries.
  Default ranking is vector similarity + a filename boost; an experimental
  hybrid mode (`--hybrid` / `EMBER_HYBRID=1`) fuses a BM25 lexical ranking
  (measured tradeoff, see "Honest capability notes").
- `ask` — answers questions with citations. With an OpenAI-compatible chat
  endpoint configured, answers are synthesized by the model — and Ember
  validates every citation marker against the chunks it actually retrieved,
  strips bogus ones (and says it did), and passes model abstentions through
  untouched. Without a chat model, `ask` is honestly labeled retrieval-only:
  ranked, line-numbered sources, and zero-score chunks are never presented
  as relevant. If a synthesis call fails, the failure is disclosed and the
  extractive answer is served instead.
- `repo_map` — entry points, hub files (most referenced), key symbols,
  languages. The orientation pass an agent otherwise burns minutes on.
- `decisions` / `recent_changes` — the "why": decision-like commits and
  ADR-style docs, plus recent history.
- `index_status` — freshness and embedder info.
- `save_note` / `recall_notes` — cross-session agent memory: an agent leaves a
  short factual note (decision, gotcha, task state) and any later session —
  including a different agent — recalls it. Notes persist in
  `.ember/notes.jsonl`; recall is deterministic keyword matching.

## Quickstart

```bash
npm install
npm test          # builds, then runs the suite (hermetic from a fresh clone)

# index any repo
node dist/cli.js index --path /path/to/repo

# search it
node dist/cli.js search "how are neighbors selected in the vector index" --path /path/to/repo

# ask with citations
node dist/cli.js ask "where does scanning decide which files to skip" --path /path/to/repo

# repo orientation
node dist/cli.js map --path /path/to/repo
node dist/cli.js decisions --path /path/to/repo

# leave a note for the next session, and recall notes later
node dist/cli.js note "chose jwt over sessions; see auth.ts" --tags auth --path /path/to/repo
node dist/cli.js notes -q auth --path /path/to/repo

# re-index after edits: only changed files are re-embedded
node dist/cli.js index --path /path/to/repo
```

## Local web UI

```bash
node dist/cli.js ui --path /path/to/repo --port 4173
# open http://127.0.0.1:4173
```

A single-page app over the real engine: search, ask, repo map, and notes.
Hit cards show the actual code with line numbers; clicking a `file:line`
citation expands the surrounding context. It binds `127.0.0.1` only, serves
source read-only and jailed to the indexed root (traversal, absolute paths
and symlink escapes are refused), and rejects cross-origin mutations. Deep
links: `http://127.0.0.1:4173/#q=...&go=search|ask`.

## Use it from your coding agent (MCP)

Ember speaks MCP over stdio. Add it to your agent's MCP config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ember": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/ember/dist/cli.js", "serve", "--path", "/path/to/your/repo"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then ask your agent to call `index_repo` once, and `repo_map` / `search_code`
/ `ask` whenever it would otherwise grope around the tree.

## LLM configuration (optional)

Everything above works offline. For semantic embeddings and synthesized
answers, point Ember at any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenRouter, Ollama, …):

```bash
export EMBER_API_BASE=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
export EMBER_API_KEY=...
export EMBER_EMBED_MODEL=<an embedding model>   # semantic embeddings
export EMBER_EMBED_DIM=<its dimension>
export EMBER_CHAT_MODEL=<a chat model>          # synthesized answers
node dist/cli.js index --full --path /path/to/repo   # re-embed with the new embedder
```

(`EMBER_CHAT_BASE` is still honored as a legacy alias for `EMBER_API_BASE`.)

**Usage accounting and request guards.** Every provider call is appended to
`.ember/usage.jsonl` and summarized by `node dist/cli.js usage`:
provider-reported token counts are recorded exactly; when a provider returns
no usage object, a chars/4 approximation is recorded and explicitly labeled
`estimated`. The API key is never logged. `EMBER_MAX_CALLS` caps provider
requests per process and `EMBER_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` caps input size per call —
both genuinely block the requests they name, but they are **request guards,
not spending limits**: Ember never sees billing; actual spend is only on your
provider's dashboard.

_Status: the endpoint paths are integration-tested against an in-process
mock OpenAI-compatible server (dimensions, retries, guards, usage records,
failure fallback). Live provider verification with real models is pending a
user-approved API budget; the offline configuration above is the verified
one. A configured endpoint receives the text it embeds or answers over (code
chunks and queries). Token counts in the usage log are not billing -
provider-reported or estimated, real spend is decided by posted prices,
routing, caching and discounts on the provider's side._

## Honest capability notes

- **Default embedder is lexical, not semantic.** Out of the box Ember uses a
  deterministic hashing embedder (stemmed token overlap). It matches shared
  vocabulary well — code identifiers are meaningful — but it does not
  paraphrase.
- **Measured retrieval quality (offline).** A 15-question sanity check about
  this repo — not a benchmark. Metrics: top-1/top-5 file accuracy and MRR;
  the corpus is frozen for each comparison; the question file itself is
  excluded via `.emberignore`, but demo/docs legitimately contain
  near-identical phrasing, so each question also runs paraphrased. Default
  engine: verbatim top-1 5/15, top-5 12/15, MRR 0.489; **paraphrase top-1
  3/15, top-5 5/15, MRR 0.230**. On these 15 questions, rewording cuts
  accuracy sharply — concrete evidence of the lexical ceiling on this
  corpus (not a universal bound), and the motivation for semantic
  embeddings. Hybrid mode (BM25 fused at lexical weight 0.25, `--hybrid` /
  `EMBER_HYBRID=1`) trades top-5 for top-1 on verbatim queries
  (6/11/0.493) — a tradeoff, not a win, so it stays opt-in. Reproduce:
  `node scripts/eval.mjs`.
- **HNSW is exact HNSW, not a placeholder.** M=16, efConstruction=200,
  diversity-preserving neighbor selection (paper alg. 4), serialized graph in
  `.ember/`. Tests measure recall@10 vs brute force (>0.9 on clustered data).
- **Incremental indexing is hash-based.** `.ember/files.json` stores a sha1
  per file. Unchanged files keep their chunks and vectors; modified files are
  re-chunked and re-embedded; deleted files are removed. Switching embedders
  (kind or dimension) triggers an automatic full rebuild.
- **Note recall is keyword matching.** `recall_notes` scores by unique
  query-term overlap — predictable and offline, not semantic.
- **Local-first.** The index never leaves your machine; network calls happen
  only when you configure an external endpoint.

## How it fits together

```
src/core/scanner.ts    git-aware file walk + .emberignore (skips deps, build output, binaries)
src/core/chunker.ts    symbol-aware code chunking (falls back to windows)
src/core/embedder.ts   pluggable embedders (offline lexical / HTTP endpoint)
src/core/llm.ts        OpenAI-compatible client: retries, request guards, usage records
src/core/hybrid.ts     BM25 lexical scorer + reciprocal rank fusion (opt-in)
src/core/hnsw.ts       pure-TS HNSW index (cosine, diversity selection)
src/core/store.ts      .ember/ persistence (chunks + vectors + graph + file hashes)
src/core/notes.ts      cross-session agent notes (notes.jsonl)
src/core/engine.ts     load + search (default and hybrid paths)
src/core/repomap.ts    structure / entry points / hub files
src/core/decisions.ts  decision log + recent changes from git
src/core/ask.ts        cited answers (validated synthesis or labeled retrieval-only)
src/mcp/server.ts      MCP server (stdio)
src/ui/server.ts       local web app backend (read-only, repo-jailed, CSRF-guarded)
src/ui/page.ts         single-page UI (no external assets)
src/cli.ts             CLI
```

See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the design in depth and `docs/ROADMAP.md` for
where it is going.

## Live demo (browser)

`demo-web/` is a static, read-only demo that runs Ember's real search engine
in the browser: it fetches the published `.ember` index artifacts of this
repo, rebuilds the HNSW graph client-side, and scores with the exact same
code path as `EmberEngine.search` (parity is enforced by
`test/demo-web.test.ts`). Retrieval is the default offline lexical mode —
no data leaves the browser.

```bash
npm run build:demo   # emits demo-web/dist (index.html + ESM + data/)
```

Deployed via GitHub Pages from the `gh-pages` branch.

# Ember architecture

One paragraph: Ember indexes a repo into symbol-aware chunks, embeds each
chunk, stores everything under `<repo>/.ember/`, and answers queries through
an HNSW approximate nearest-neighbour search plus (optionally) an
OpenAI-compatible chat model that is only ever shown retrieved chunks. The
same engine serves three frontends: the CLI, an MCP stdio server for coding
agents, and a local web UI.

## Pipeline

```
scan -> chunk -> embed -> HNSW -> persist (.ember/)
                                 |
        +------------------------+------------------------+
        |                        |                        |
      CLI                 MCP server (stdio)        ember ui (127.0.0.1)
```

1. **Scan** (`scanner.ts`): deterministic walk (byte-sorted by path so chunk
   ids are reproducible), skipping dependencies, build output, binaries,
   oversized files, lockfiles, and anything in `.emberignore`. Language from
   extension; 256 KB per-file cap; 4000-file total cap.
2. **Chunk** (`chunker.ts`): symbol-aware - functions/classes/methods become
   chunks with their line ranges and symbol names; files without recognizable
   symbols fall back to overlapping windows. Chunks carry
   `file / startLine / endLine / symbol / text`, which is what makes
   `file:line` citations exact.
3. **Embed** (`embedder.ts`): pluggable.
   - Default `HashingEmbedder`: deterministic, offline, lexical. Tokenizes
     code (camelCase/snake_case split, light stemming) and hashes tokens into
     a 1024-dim vector (FNV-1a, signed slots, log TF). Matches shared
     vocabulary; does not paraphrase.
   - Optional `HttpEmbedder`: any OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint.
     The returned dimension is validated against `EMBER_EMBED_DIM` - a
     mismatch fails loudly instead of corrupting the store.
4. **Index** (`hnsw.ts`): pure-TypeScript HNSW (M=16, efConstruction=200,
   cosine, diversity-preserving neighbor selection = paper algorithm 4).
   Tests measure recall@10 against brute force (>0.9 on clustered data).
5. **Persist** (`store.ts`): `meta.json`, `chunks.jsonl`, `vectors.f32`
   (row-major, aligned with chunk ids), `hnsw.json`, `files.json` (per-file
   sha1 for incremental re-index), `notes.jsonl`, `usage.jsonl`. Reads are
   hardened against torn/corrupt tails; the notes tail is repaired before
   append.

## Retrieval

Default path (`engine.ts`): embed the query, pull `3k` HNSW candidates,
rescore by exact dot product, add a capped filename-token boost, cut to k.

Experimental hybrid path (`--hybrid` / `EMBER_HYBRID=1`): fuse the vector
ranking with a BM25 ranking (chunk text + filename tokens) using reciprocal
rank fusion, lexical leg weighted 0.25. Measured on the 15-question sanity
eval over the current corpus (a sanity check, not a benchmark: 15 questions,
one corpus, ±1 is noise). Default: verbatim top-1 5/15, top-5 12/15, MRR
0.489; paraphrased top-1 3/15, top-5 5/15, MRR 0.230. Hybrid: verbatim
6/11/0.493 - a tradeoff, not a win, so it is opt-in. The paraphrase collapse
quantifies the lexical embedder's core limitation and motivates semantic
embeddings (M2). Equal weighting was measured and rejected (top-5 13 -> 10
on the earlier corpus: exact-match ranking over-rewards files that echo
query phrasing).

## Answer synthesis (`ask.ts`)

Retrieval always comes first: the model only ever sees the top-k retrieved
chunks, numbered. The system prompt forbids inventing code and requires
`[n]` citations. After the model answers, Ember:

- validates every `[n]` marker against the retrieved set - out-of-range
  markers are stripped and the stripping is disclosed;
- passes abstention ("the chunks don't contain the answer") through
  untouched;
- appends the Sources list itself (citations are never model-authored);
- on any provider failure, discloses it and serves the extractive answer.

Without a chat model, `ask` is labeled retrieval-only, excerpts are

## Provider client (`llm.ts`)

One `LlmClient` for chat + embeddings: 60s timeout, a single retry with 1s
backoff on transient statuses (408/409/425/429/5xx), honest errors otherwise.
Every call appends a usage record to `.ember/usage.jsonl`:
provider-reported token counts exactly; chars/4 estimates explicitly labeled
`estimated`. The API key is sent to the configured endpoint as a bearer
header and never logged.

`EMBER_MAX_CALLS` and `EMBER_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` are process-level request
guards: they block the named request, and their error messages say so.
`EMBER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` caps synthesized answer length (default 1024).
Requests are serialized per client instance (concurrency 1, enforced by an
in-process queue); the web UI shares one client across requests so the cap
and queue hold globally there. None of this tracks
or limits spending: Ember has no access to provider billing, and logged
token counts (provider-reported or estimated) are never converted to
dollars.

## Trust and security model

- **Local-first.** With no endpoint configured there is zero network I/O.
- **What a configured endpoint sees:** the text it embeds (code chunks and
  queries) and the chunks sent for answer synthesis. Nothing else leaves the
  machine. The key lives only in the environment / process memory.
- **ember ui** binds `127.0.0.1` only. Source files are served read-only and
  jailed to the indexed root by realpath resolution - `../`, absolute paths
  and symlinks pointing outside are refused (tested). Non-GET requests with
  a cross-site `Origin` are refused (CSRF guard). Responses are `nosniff`.
- **MCP** runs over stdio; the parent process controls it. Tool args are
  validated with zod.
- **The browser demo** is static and read-only: it fetches this repo's
  published index artifacts and runs the same search code client-side.

## Testing strategy

47 tests, hermetic from a fresh clone (`npm test` builds first). Provider
behavior is tested against an in-process mock OpenAI-compatible server, so
the LLM layer is fully verified with zero real calls. MCP is tested through
real stdio sessions. The web UI has API-level workflow + security tests and
an opt-in real-Chrome e2e (`npm run e2e:ui`). The browser demo's parity with
the engine is asserted by serving the demo over HTTP and comparing hits and
scores exactly.

# Ember roadmap: from hackathon prototype to primary project

Ember started as a 24-hour hackathon build. This roadmap turns it into a
full-fledged, LLM-backed, end-to-end project. Ordering is by leverage:
retrieval quality first, then the interface, then proof.

## M0 - Honest foundations (done)

- [x] `npm test` is hermetic on a fresh clone (was 3 failing MCP tests).

## M1 - Real LLM layer, zero-spend tested (done)

- [x] `LlmClient`: OpenAI-compatible chat + embeddings with timeouts, one
      retry on transient errors, and process-level request guards
      (`EMBER_MAX_CALLS`, `EMBER_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS`). These guards block
      requests; they are NOT billing limits - real spend is only ever on
      the provider's dashboard.
- [x] Usage accounting in `.ember/usage.jsonl` + `ember usage` command.
      Provider-reported tokens recorded exactly; chars/4 approximations
      labeled estimated. The API key is never logged.
- [x] `ask`: citation markers validated against retrieved chunks (bogus
      ones stripped, stripping disclosed), model abstention preserved,
      extractive fallback with the failure disclosed on API errors.
- [x] Hybrid retrieval built but OPT-IN (`--hybrid` / `EMBER_HYBRID=1`):
      HNSW vector ranking fused with BM25 (chunk text + filename tokens)
      via weighted RRF (lexical 0.25). Measured on the 15-question
      same-repo sanity eval, old engine vs hybrid on the same corpus:
      top-1 5 -> 6, top-5 13 -> 12, MRR .502 -> .510. Top-5 regressing
      means it is a tradeoff, not a win, so the pre-hybrid ranking stays
      the default until semantic embeddings make the two legs genuinely
      diverge (M2). Equal weighting was measured and rejected outright
      (top-5 13 -> 10). Caveats: 15 questions, one corpus, +/-1 is noise.
- [x] All LLM behavior tested against an in-process mock OpenAI server.
      44/44 tests, zero real provider calls.

## M2 - Live provider verification (blocked: needs an approved API budget)

- [ ] Verify embeddings + chat against OpenRouter with real models;
      measure and report per-call token usage (provider-reported).
- [ ] Re-run the retrieval sanity check with real embeddings; publish the
      before/after (same frozen corpus, verbatim + paraphrase rows).
- [ ] Re-check current model IDs and pricing at verification time - do not
      trust remembered ones.

Spend discipline for the paid run (authority-critical):
- EMBER_MAX_CALLS caps REQUEST COUNT, never dollars; an approved dollar
  amount cannot be mapped to a request count without conservative,
  currently-verified token and pricing figures covering retries, embedding
  batches and provider routing differences.
- Before the first paid call: confirm the account/key's available credit
  and current pricing from the provider itself, prefer a provider-enforced
  spend cap on the key where available, and compute a maximum aggregate
  token envelope for the scoped run. Stop and escalate if the run cannot
  be bounded within the approved amount.
- Proposed (unverified until then): qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b (dim 4096,
  $0.01/M tokens listed 2026-10-28) and qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507
  ($0.09/M in, $0.30/M out listed 2026-10-28). Estimates, not bounds.
